purpose: Make high-value experience discovery and candidateization fail-closed before closeout. The candidate pool checker only validates already-recorded candidates; this policy decides when a task must explicitly judge whether new Evolution candidates are required.

claim_boundary.near_100_percent_goal: Every Layer B task with review, governance, architecture, release-safety, bug-fix, user-correction, Prism, test-failure, closeout-blocker, process-storm, recursion, privacy or security signals must include an Evolution Factory candidate handling section before receipt.
claim_boundary.not_claimed: This policy does not let scripts semantically understand all natural language or auto-write active identity. It forces a visible candidate/no-promote decision for high-signal tasks.

signal_groups.meaning: The user corrected, challenged, interrupted, or exposed a workflow miss.
A failed check, regression, or acceptance finding changed the implementation.
The task touched closeout, receipt, pending closure, or completion truth.
Independent review or red-team evidence is involved.
Runtime behavior can create loops, process leaks, stale children, or resource storms.
Release, package, privacy, secret, or public-surface risk is involved.

accepted_outcomes: deferred-with-owner with owner and next trigger
release_readiness_rule: Formal release readiness may not proceed to publication while the Evolution harvest signal gate is unresolved for the release task or any current pre-release hard-gate task.
fallback_rule: If the checker cannot prove whether a high-signal task needs candidate handling, fail closed and require the report section rather than silently skipping.
